input.standard: ASTM E741 (concentration decay, single zone); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the volume of air served by /habitat/lab/eclss/scrubber-1-v5, from a gentle CO2 rise (40% speed) then a decay at full speed, with the hatch closed throughout.

monitoring.reason: CDR left the band in the previous rise; both Lab occupants breathe the raised CO2 and are watched for the whole test.

steps.why: Rise: reduced scrubber flow (effective ~0.4 m3/min) lets Lab CO2 climb gently from 950 ppm toward ~1900 ppm equilibrium; CDR and FE-3 held at rest.
Decay: full speed (Qe 1 m3/min), about one time constant for V~30 m3 (tau ~30 min); record CO2 each minute and fit C_eq + (C0-C_eq)exp(-t/tau).

abort.when: the device refuses a step's command
CDR or FE-3 out of the 45-120 bpm band, monitoring lost, or one more person in the Lab

expected.rise: Predicted with a first guess V=30 m3 (default, stated as such), 2 awake occupants at 0.38 L/min each (~25 ppm/min at zero scrubbing): at 40% speed Qe~0.4 m3/min, tau~75 min, equilibrium ~1900 ppm; after 20 min CO2 about 1150-1200 ppm, a rise of ~200-250 ppm, staying well under co2MaxPpm 2000. Refuted if CO2 rises much faster (smaller V or hatch leak) or does not rise (larger V, exchange with Hab-B).
expected.decay: At full speed Qe=1 m3/min, tau=V/Qe~30 min plus 3.33 min scrubber lag; CO2 falls toward ~760 ppm above outdoor level; fit gives tau and V=Qe*tau. Hypotheses fail if the fit residuals are systematic, tau is not stable between the first and second half, or Hab-B CO2 moves in step with the Lab's (opening exchanging air).
expected.vitals: CDR and FE-3 stay within 45-120 bpm; at ~1200 ppm no physiological effect is expected. A breach would show the cause is not CO2 alone (activity or the simulation).

hypotheses: The Lab is one well-mixed zone.
The closed hatch exchanges no significant air with Hab-B: not measured, only watched through Hab-B's CO2 sensors.
Occupants' number (2) and activity (rest, ~0.38 L/min each) are constant during the test; production is not measured.
Scrubber effective flow at full speed is the datasheet's 1 m3/min, and about 0.4 m3/min at 40% (linear in speed, assumed).
The first guess V=30 m3 is only used to size durations, not to compute the result.
The rise may be only ~200-250 ppm, marginal over sensor noise; accepted to keep the crew's exposure low.
